package.json: engines block and full dependency list

node_X_constraint_notes: base repo declares Node >=22.23.4 <23 in package.json engines — this is a hard project policy (not an upstream framework minimum)

next 12.1.0 package manifest self-declares engines node >=12.22.0 (verified by fetching the published tarball during this scout run); the <23 upper bound is therefore the project's own pin, not something Next requires, and can be re-declared freely in the Nuxt 3 package.json
source-baseline.json notes the host did not have Node 22 installed and ran with --ignore-engines; the scout flags this as a clean-environment gap, not as an endorse of running the benchmark off-range

Nuxt 3 does not mandate a specific Node version and supports Node 22; the repo's engines block >=22.23.4 <23 is project policy, not a framework floor. No Node downgrade is required by the migration. The scout does not assume whether the upper <23 bound is retained or widened — that is a work-package decision for WP-1.

safe_nuxt3_topology.framework: Nuxt 3 (Vite-based, Nitro server engine) with Vue 3 Composition API and strict TypeScript
directory_rationale: pages/*.tsx (including all API routes under pages/api/) are all replaced by Nuxt's pages/ + server/ split, so the API directory must move to server/api/ to match Nitro conventions and keep the server-only credential boundary explicit
contexts/TelnyxMeetContext.ts and contexts/DebugContext.ts map to composables/ + stores/ (a reactive module or provide/inject also works)

utils/ (parsePhoneNumber.ts, storage.ts, userMedia.ts, virtualBackground.ts, helpers.ts) all import browser/globals-free logic, but helpers.ts specifically imports Notify from lib/bugsnag.js — that import is safe only because Bugsnag's notify() no-ops if no API key is configured, and the scout cannot verify that at build time without a rebuild. Do not assume no split is required; verify at migration time.
components/ are migrated to .vue SFCs; styled-components usage must be replaced because accepted scopes say no styled-components runtime

pwa_topology.assets: public/manifest.json, public/icon-192x192.png, public/icon-512x512.png stay at the same public path; the PWA is built with NODE_ENV=production (build:pwa script). This scout did not read next.config.js for a workbox/sw.js block because it was only partially quoted in the mission context — the scout cannot confirm whether a service worker is emitted today without a full build, only that .gitignore already ignores public/sw.js and workbox-*.js. If Nuxt PWA output is needed, @vite-pwa/nuxt or a manually-authored sw/ module is a decision for the topology package, not this build-system scope.

state_courses: TelnyxMeetContext.ts and DebugContext.ts are currently React contexts wrapping React state; the Nuxt replacement is either (a) a Nuxt store (Pinia is not present in the current dependency set, so adding it is a new dependency decision) for TelnyxMeetContext and a simple ref for DebugContext, or (b) provide/inject with a composable that holds reactive refs — choice is a design decision outside this scout's build-system scope, but the scout flags it as a write-set boundary: the replacement files live under stores/ or composables/, not contexts/

next_runtime_to_remove: next-env.d.ts (framework-generated, deleted with the Next.js stack)
dependency_replacements.puppeteer_observation: puppeteer ^23.1.0 is a production dependency today; this scout's read of pages/, components/, utils/, hooks/, .github/workflows/ and the package.json scripts found no invocation of it and no relevant devtool in next.config.js — it is carried as an apparently unused/heavy production dep. Dropping it or moving it to devDependencies is a legitimate part of the dependency-cleanup package, but the scout flags it as an observation, not as a forced change, because the workspace may use it in a way the scout did not cover.

bugsnag_adapter_change.current: @bugsnag/plugin-react (React-specific integration) + webpack-bugsnag-plugins + @zeit/next-source-maps (error-reporting stack whose source-map upload is baked into next.config.js webpack handling)
bugsnag_adapter_change.note: There is no drop-in Nuxt/Web-vue equivalent for the webpack-bugsnag-plugins source-map uploader; the migration should either (a) keep @bugsnag/js and drop the automated source-map uploader (error stack traces become less readable, which is a real behavior tradeoff) or (b) find an equivalent uploader for Nuxt's .output/. The scout flags this as an explicit judgment boundary, not as a default-drop.

keep_as_is: @telnyx/video 1.0.1 (pinned, no semantic drift in the migration) — browser-only SDK; the Nuxt 3 SSR nitro layer must not import it unguarded at top-level in any file SSR-rendered; the mission brief explicitly says the boundary must be typed and lifecycle-safe, which implies the scout's 'keep as is' does not mean keep as-is at the import site — a thin typed adapter (see mission-brief included_scope item 4) is required to wrap it behind composables and ensure no SSR access. That wrapper is out of the build-scoped work packages but is a prerequisite the build-scoped package must assume when it removes the old direct imports.
dependency_replacements.lockfile_constraint: yarn.lock is a Yarn v1 lockfile; Nuxt 3 works with Yarn v1 but Yarn berry (v3/v4, PnP or node_modules linker) is the modern default. If the venue keeps Yarn v1, the lockfile must be fully regenerated after dependency changes — the scout does not pre-generate it, only records this constraint.

server_only_credential_boundary.invariant: TELNYX_API_KEY and TELNYX_CALL_CONTROL_API_HOST are required by server routes only and must never appear in any client-visible config, env sample, or bundle output

server_reads: pages/api/refresh_client_token.ts: process.env.TELNYX_API_HOST only (the browser supplies the refresh token upstream; this route carries no Authorization header, unlike the other token route)
current_state.client_exposure: none found in the mission-visible codebase; .env.sample has empty values only
current_state.source_baseline_confirms: source-baseline.json confirms install/lint/build all ran cleanly with no secret present in source

server_only_credential_boundary.nuxt3_binding: In Nuxt, runtimeConfig private keys bind server-side only: useRuntimeConfig().telnxApiKey is server-bound and nuxt.config.ts must set envKey: 'TELNYX_API_KEY' so it reads process.env at server runtime, never baked into a client bundle
server_only_credential_boundary.credential_claims_policy: No value from .env.sample or any real env variable is copied into this scout artifact. Gloable variable names and host defaults (api.telnyx.com/v2 from .env.sample) are recorded; if .env.sample ever holds a real key it must be flagged and the value never copied.

route_migration_concerns: pages/api/rooms/[roomId].ts is a dynamic route on roomId; Nuxt's server/api/rooms/[roomId].get.ts preserves this 1:1

pages/api/client_token.ts checks req.body.room_id but pages/api/refresh_client_token.ts checks req.body.refresh_token and uses req.body.room_id as a path param without validating it — the refresh route does not verify room_id presence, so any caller with a valid refresh_token can use it against any room; the scout records this as a behavior to preserve as-is (per benchmark rule on source defects), not as a defect to fix during migration.

pages/rooms/[roomId].tsx and pages/rooms/index.tsx use query-parameter-driven state (roomId, roomId, client_token, refresh_token) — the Nuxt Vue SFC equivalents preserve query params via useRoute().query; the scout notes the query param casing must be preserved exactly because the accepted criteria say query params must continue to work

dial_out.ts sends video_room_context as a JSON string inside the JSON body (double-serialized); the Vue migration must not 'fix' this unless a regression test proves the original behavior, per the benchmark rule about source defects

pages/rooms/list.tsx and pages/rooms/index.tsx and pages/index.tsx are separate routes — Nuxt map them to pages/rooms/list.vue, pages/rooms/index.vue, pages/index.vue respectively, preserving nesting so deep links still work
